item.description:
Originally published on Substack.

All the good stuff I read and learned last month, plus a few things from November.

Every major AI launch already makes it to human consciousness through 24x7 influencers rambling about it. We’ve become numb to it.

Models editing models

Craziest thing I came across was GPT-6 Astra editing Qwen3.5-0.8B’s weights. It changed just 0.016% of them and raised its MATH-500 score from 7.9% to 48.1%, without a training loop.

item.title: Only DSA roadmap you’ll ever need
item.description:
Originally published on Substack.

Why does this exist?

Life has too many good things. DSA prep is not one of them.

But you need to clear DSA interviews to get a tech job. Most of the roadmaps out there are link spams with bazillion boring problems.

DSA is not going anywhere for 3-4 years at least. As it is the easiest way to scale the interview pipeline.

In other words it is the easiest way to filter candidates out on raw problem solving skills.

item.title: LLM math every software engineer must know
item.description:
Originally published on Substack.

Most engineers interact with LLMs daily, yet many struggle to estimate the basic resource profile of the models they use. Here are four mental models to help you put model size, intelligence, memory footprint, and training costs into perspective.

Without being too sciency.

I. Model size: Parameters != IQ

Models are categorized by their parameter count: 8B, 70B, 405B. A “parameter” is essentially a single learned weight or bias in a neural network.

item.title: Links #5
item.description:
Originally published on Substack.

Changing std:sort at Google’s scale

How many reasonably fast sorting algorithms do you know about? If you use any modern language, there is a high chance that it has its own implementation of sort which houses multiple algorithms and uses their combination to achieve consistent performance irrespective of the input.

This post is about the internals of sort in both LLVM and GNU. How the author improved LLVM’s std:sort, what kind of problem-solving and experimentation goes into such initiatives, and very satisfying animation that pitches different combinations of sorting algorithms against each other.

item.title: Solving A XOR operation - Hackerearth
item.description:
For context, link to the problem being discussed.

Solution that passes

  • Let’s say $X = e_1\oplus e_2\oplus\cdots \oplus e_n$ i.e. XOR of all elements of $S$. If it satisfies the condition of being $k$ then it is the answer, otherwise no answer exists.

Why is it so?

  • One thing is for sure that every element will be mapped to some other element in the set.

  • If the answer is $k$ then $a_i$ will be mapped to $a_i\oplus k$. So what we can do is we can check to which element, first element of the set will be mapped, i.e. try every possible pair with first element and check if so formed $k$ is the answer. Mind that $k$ will always be positive as there is no repetition in a set.

item.title: Basic ffmpeg reference
item.description:
1. Converting to some format

ffmpeg -i input.mp3 output.m4a

2. Merging audio and video

  • Can change final container (mkv is most versatile), ffmpeg automatically decides the decoders for the job.
ffmpeg -i audio.mp3 -i video.mp4 -c copy merged_video.mkv

3. Keeping Output quality same as Input quality (-sameq)

ffmpeg -i input.avi -sameq output.mkv

4. Convert only first 30 seconds (-t)

ffmpeg -i aadat.mp3 -t 30 aadatintro.mp3
  • -t also supports hh:mm:ss as time format
  • Variation of this can be used to cut a part of the video, -ss flag sets the start time. So set the start time with -ss and duration with -t
ffmpeg -i aadat.mp3 -ss 1:12 -t 1:00 solo.mp3

5. Strip audio or video

  • -an removes audio and -vn strips video
ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn audio.mp3

6. Bitrate

  • -ab sets the audio bitrate and -b sets the video bitrate explicitly
ffmpeg -i audio.mp3 -ab 128k audiocompressed.mp3

Notes

  • default bitrate for video is 200kbps and 64 kbps for audio
  • ffmpeg options are always applied to next file in argument list, can be input or ouput file.
  • RTFM for more
